Why Birangonas not given state honour in 43 years
2014-01-28T00:00:00+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/why-birangonas-not-given-state-honour-in-43-years-8775

The High Court yesterday issued a rule asking the government to explain in four weeks why it should not be directed to upgrade the social status of Birangonas (war heroines) and provide them with state honour and facilities like those of freedom fighters. The government was also asked to explain why it should not be ordered to prepare a comprehensive list of Birangonas, who were victimised during the country's Liberation War in 1971, and to issue a gazette to this effect by March 26. The rule came in response to a writ petition, which sought such directives from the HC. The authorities concerned were also asked to explain why the silence of the government about this issue for the last 43 years after independence should not be declared illegal. Seven government high officials, including secretaries to the ministries of law, liberation war affairs, and finance, were directed to respond to the rule, Deputy Attorney General Mokhlesur Rahman told The Daily Star. The bench of Justice Salma Masud Chowdhury and Justice Md Habibul Gani came up with the rule after hearing the writ petition jointly filed last week by Salma Ali, executive director of Bangladesh National Women Lawyers Association (BNWLA), and Mitali Hossain, president of the alumni association of Saleha Ihsaque Girls High School. The petitioners said Birangonas were tortured and victimised during the Liberation War, and they had played an important role in achieving independence, but they were not recognised and given any state honour in 43 years. Fawzia Karim Firoze appeared for the petitioners.
